chris: Hey team, streaming chat gets cut mid-generation despite setting timeout=120. Sometimes see 504/connection reset. Repro below.
marie (support): Sorry you're hitting this — are you using streaming responses or buffering? which py sdk version? any quick code + logs?
chris: streaming. minimal repro:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="REDACTED", timeout=120)
with c.chat.stream(model="gpt-4-like", input="long prompt...") as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text)
```
logs:
```
ERROR chunk read timeout after 30s
ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
```
marie (support): thanks. can you paste `pip show redwood-inference` and whether you're behind a proxy or using our hosted api?
chris: pip show -> Version: 0.3.1
we're calling hosted API in us-west-2, no proxy. traffic pattern: long generations ~120s, sometimes ~200s
eli (eng-runtime): FYI older 0.3.x uses a single `timeout` param that was applied to connect/read differently vs what's documented for 0.4+. there's a known issue where streaming applies the per-chunk deadline instead of a total stream deadline -> long gens can see repeated chunk timeouts and connection resets, leaving sockets in TIME_WAIT and exhausting pool.
eli (eng-runtime): quick checks: 1) try upgrading to 0.4.2+ 2) as a workaround, set a higher read/stream timeout via httpx Timeout or pass the new `timeouts` dict if available.
chris: can you show example for workaround? upgrading is blocked by constraints atm
eli (eng-runtime): example:
```python
import httpx
from redwood import Client
httpx_timeout = httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=300.0)
c = Client(api_key="...", httpx_client=httpx.Client(timeout=httpx_timeout))
```
this forces a long read timeout for the whole stream. also ensure your httpx client isn't reusing a pool with too-small `limits`.
sara (sre): saw similar pattern in infra — aborted streams left many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT under the older sdk. we've applied a short-term nginx keepalive tweak and will monitor.
chris: thanks. if we upgrade will there be breaking changes to our call signatures? worried about tests
eli (eng-runtime): 0.4.x has minimal surface changes for chat/stream. main change is how timeouts are passed; migration notes in the changelog. if you can't upgrade, we'll backport the streaming-total-timeout fix to a 0.3.x patch — need to know how many customers are impacted.
marie (support): I'm escalating to eng and SRE. opening ticket INF-5123, marking P2 and linking this thread. cc @eli @sara. Also asking billing to check if these resets caused duplicate billing for aborted tokens.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime/ingest v2026.03.16-821
chris: appreciate it. leaving logs and a full HAR in the ticket. will try the httpx workaround in staging and report back :thumbsup:
eli (eng-runtime): great — if you can share socket stats (`ss -s` or `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l`) that'll help us quantify pool exhaustion.
chris: ran `ss -s` -> TIME-WAIT ~4200, established ~10. added to ticket.
marie (support): thank you — we'll follow up in INF-5123. for anyone finding this thread: short-term fixes = upgrade to 0.4.2+, or instantiate your own httpx Client with a long read timeout; long-term fix = backport and patch to 0.3.x. :white_check_mark:
